instruction: Create a requirements.txt file in the project root directory.

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a requirements.txt file for Python dependencies. Evaluator uses partial scoring: 0.5 for file existence with content, 1.0 for having at least one valid package specification line (e.g., 'requests==2.28.0' or 'numpy').

llm_judge_reasons: Expected value 'rules.has_valid_format=true' is never used by the metric function - the 'rules' parameter is received but completely ignored in the function logic

Package validation logic is too permissive at vscode.py:41 - checks if ANY character is alphanumeric in the first part before '=/</>!/!', which would accept nonsense strings like 'hello world' or 'asdfasdf' as valid packages
Metric gives 0.5 score for file with only whitespace/comments (no actual package specs), which doesn't meaningfully fulfill the instruction to create a requirements.txt file
No verification that package specifications follow standard format (package-name==version or package-name>=version) - just checks if alphanumeric characters exist
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Make the metric function actually use the 'rules' parameter to check 'has_valid_format' condition

Improve package validation logic to properly check requirements.txt format using regex like '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+(==|>=|<=|>|<|!=|~=)[0-9.]+' or at minimum verify line contains package name and version specifier
Consider requiring at least one actual package specification line (not just content) for any score above 0.0
Add edge case handling for common invalid content (e.g., only whitespace, only comments) to return 0.0 score

metric check_requirements_txt__6ee0182d second parameter type (dict) may not match expected.rules type (Dict)
